svg.title: L App process lifecycle light
svg.desc: A typical successful App process flow is Build, Run, Await, then reading Output. Build checks readiness of artifacts built ahead of time. Run launches an App process and returns after acknowledgment; it does not wait for completion. Await joins and executes that invocation continuation inline once. Output is raw finalized stdout and never implicitly waits. Optional Stop requests forceful termination; use Await to join. Start and Execute are source-defined App compositions. App-owned Services provide library artifacts; standalone Service declarations create no artifact or process.

g.data-label: Build, Run, Stop, Await, Output and Error apply to Apps.
